chapter: Family, Margaret's story and Eutris's memories
title: The mission church and Sunday school denominations
summary: Eutris describes the missionary Sunday school, the denominations involved and Methodist church-going.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: When you first started playing, what songs, what kind of music did they play at the mission?
Tuck Me to Sleep in. My Old Kentucky Home.
But what was the purpose of playing - was it in church services or what kind of functions did you play?
It was a Sunday school and he wanted to create a band and put this group together. So that's what he did.
Well, he was really just interested, I think, in the children in the neighborhood Sunday school in the afternoon;
... (NOT CLEAR) ... They had all white teachers.
Do you know what denomination that was, what kind of church it was?
It was more than just one, because there were Baptist children went to that Sunday school. He was a Methodist. He was a member of the Methodist Church and so was I. We went there in the morning.
You and Jay C. are Methodists?

Yes, then. I'm Lutheran now. So then after all of the children in the neighborhood left their Sunday school - Methodist, Baptist, Presbyterian (there was a little Presbyterian church there too) - then in the afternoons we all gathered at this hall to missionary Sunday School.
But you don't know what denomination that particular one was?
No, I really don't, because the only thing I do know is that they were missionaries because one of the women was trying to get some of the girls interested in going to Africa.
